rv.q: Directed with swagger and finesse by Matthew Xia, Dave Harris’s play explores sex, pleasure, parenthood and what makes a man
As this sharp satire swerves from sex comedy to sweet study of male intimacy, the acts they become a part of end up being less gratuitous and altogether more tender than they may have expected.
Give me this thoughtful madness over the kitchen sink equivalent any day.
Harris and director Matthew Xia give us an incredibly tender portrayal of vulnerability and driftlessness.

It’s immersive without being overbearing, setting the tone for a show that knows exactly how to work a crowd. When the troupe, Trae, Geoff, and Donnie, get to strut their stuff, the payoff is immediate. The routines are slick, sexy, and genuinely impressive, blending raw athleticism with a knowing wink.
Tender is a wildly entertaining play that balances comedy with emotional depth, while sharing a unique exploration of masculinity.
Tender is another excellent drama in this space that reaches out to men who are conditioned to conform and stay quiet about their problems and any self-doubt.

cn.t: Harris's strip club drama earns praise as a sharp, affecting exploration of modern masculinity that swerves from sex comedy to sincere study of male intimacy, directed with swagger by Matthew Xia.
